comparisons.peer_summary: Loans include held for investment loans accounted for at amortized cost (net of allowance or fair value option) and held for sale loans at lower of cost or fair value. Interest is recognized on an accrual basis over the life of the loan.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS classify loans held for sale and measure them at the lower of aggregate cost or fair value. However, GS explicitly distinguishes held-for-sale loans from held-for-investment loans in its accounting methodology summary, whereas BAC's disclosure focuses specifically on the definition and valuation of LHFS without the immediate contrast to held-for-investment accounting in the cited text.

sentences.text: Loans that the Corporation intends to sell in the foreseeable future, including residential mortgages, loan syndications, and to a lesser degree, commercial real estate, consumer finance and other loans, are reported as LHFS and are carried at the lower of aggregate cost or fair value.

Loans includes (i) loans held for investment that are accounted for at amortized cost net of allowance for loan losses or at fair value under the fair value option and (ii) loans held for sale that are accounted for at the lower of cost or fair value.

comparisons.peer_topic: Loans held-for-sale measurement and valuation methodology
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans held-for-sale are measured at the lower of cost or fair value, with changes recorded in noninterest revenue. Valuation is performed on a portfolio basis for consumer loans and on an individual loan basis for wholesale loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM measure loans held for sale at the lower of cost or fair value. JPM provides additional detail on how valuation changes are recorded (in noninterest revenue) and specifies that valuation is performed on a portfolio basis for consumer loans and individually for wholesale loans, whereas BAC's disclosed text is limited to the definition and valuation basis without specifying the revenue line item or valuation granularity.

sentences.text: Loans that the Corporation intends to sell in the foreseeable future, including residential mortgages, loan syndications, and to a lesser degree, commercial real estate, consumer finance and other loans, are reported as LHFS and are carried at the lower of aggregate cost or fair value.
Loans held-for-sale are measured at the lower of cost or fair value, with valuation changes recorded in noninterest revenue.
For consumer loans, the valuation is performed on a portfolio basis.
For wholesale loans, the valuation is performed on an individual loan basis.

comparisons.peer_topic: Measurement and valuation of loans held for sale
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans held for sale are measured at the lower of amortized cost or fair value, with valuation changes recorded in Other revenues. Valuation allowances are determined individually, except for residential mortgage loans where they are determined at the loan product level, and increases in fair value above initial carrying amounts are not recognized.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS measure loans held for sale at the lower of cost (or amortized cost) or fair value. MS distinguishes itself by specifying that valuation changes are recorded in 'Other revenues' and that increases in fair value above initial carrying amounts are not recognized. Additionally, MS details that valuation allowances are determined individually, except for residential mortgage loans where they are determined at the loan product level, a granularity not present in BAC's cited definition.

sentences.text: Loans that the Corporation intends to sell in the foreseeable future, including residential mortgages, loan syndications, and to a lesser degree, commercial real estate, consumer finance and other loans, are reported as LHFS and are carried at the lower of aggregate cost or fair value.
Loans held for sale are measured at the lower of amortized cost or fair value, with valuation changes recorded in Other revenues.
The Firm determines the valuation allowance on an individual loan basis, except for residential mortgage loans for which the valuation allowance is determined at the loan product level.
Increases in fair value above initial carrying value are not recognized.
